examples.en: I boil soybean paste stew in an earthenware pot.

examples.ko: 뚝배기는 천천히 식어서 음식이 오래 따뜻해요.
examples.en: The earthenware pot cools slowly, so the food stays warm for a long time.
A sizzling hot pot came out at the restaurant.
My friend gave me a new earthenware pot as a gift.
Can I put the pot straight on the fire?

examples.ko: 추운 날에는 뚝배기 국밥이 먹고 싶어요.
examples.en: On cold days I want to eat rice soup in a hot pot.

explain: 뚝배기는 찌개나 국을 끓여서 그대로 상에 올리는 그릇이에요. 쇠 냄비보다 천천히 끓고 천천히 식어서 상에 나온 뒤에도 보글보글해요. '뚝배기보다 장맛'이라는 속담은 겉보다 속이 중요할 때 써요.
explain_en: A 뚝배기 is a pot you boil stew or soup in and bring straight to the table. It heats and cools more slowly than a metal pot, so the food keeps bubbling at the table. The proverb '뚝배기보다 장맛' means the inside matters more than the looks.

examples.en: I watched a seal show at the aquarium.
The seal balances a ball on its nose.
Seals catch and eat fish in the sea.

examples.ko: 아이들이 귀여운 물개 앞에서 사진을 찍었어요.
examples.en: The children took photos in front of the cute seal.

examples.ko: 저는 물개를 실제로 본 적이 없어요.
examples.en: I have never seen a seal in real life.
There was a child clapping like a seal.

explain: 물개는 바다에 사는 동물이에요. 수족관에서 공을 받고 박수 치는 모습으로 가장 많이 알려져 있어요. 팔을 앞으로 내밀고 손뼉을 치는 모습을 '물개 박수'라고도 말해요.
explain_en: A 물개 is a sea animal, best known from aquarium shows where it catches balls and 'claps'. People also say '물개 박수' for clapping with the arms held out in front.

en: be naked; be bare; be stripped

examples.en: The baby runs around the yard with nothing on.
A naked child is laughing in the bathhouse.

examples.ko: 동화 속 임금님은 벌거벗은 채로 거리를 걸었어요.
examples.en: The king in the fairy tale walked down the street naked.
Some people sleep with nothing on because it is hot.
In winter the bare trees look lonely.
They are planting trees on the bare mountain.

explain: 아기나 동화 속 인물에는 자연스럽지만, 어른에게 쓰면 아주 직접적으로 들려요. 같은 뜻의 '알몸'은 명사라서 '알몸으로'라고 하고, 벌거벗다는 '벌거벗은 채로'처럼 동사로 써요. 나무가 없는 산에도 '벌거벗은 산'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It sounds natural for a baby or a fairy-tale figure, but very direct for an adult. '알몸' is a noun ('알몸으로'), while 벌거벗다 is a verb ('벌거벗은 채로'). It is also used for a treeless mountain: '벌거벗은 산'.

en: bulging; protrudingly in a rounded way

examples.en: His belly is sticking out round.

examples.ko: 다람쥐가 입에 먹이를 넣어 볼을 볼록 부풀렸어요.
examples.en: The squirrel stuffed food in its mouth and puffed out its cheeks.
The balloon swelled up round.
Your pocket is bulging out.

examples.ko: 이불 속에서 고양이 등이 볼록 올라왔어요.
examples.en: A cat's back rose up in a round bump under the blanket.

examples.ko: 아이가 가방을 볼록 채워서 학교에 갔어요.
examples.en: The child went to school with a bulging bag.

explain: 볼록은 둥글게 살짝 튀어나온 모양에 써요. 더 크고 많이 튀어나오면 '불룩'을 쓰는데 느낌이 더 커요. 반대로 안쪽으로 들어간 모양은 '오목'이라고 해요.
explain_en: 볼록 describes a slight, round bulge. For something bigger and more swollen, Koreans use '불룩', which feels stronger. The opposite, a dent going inward, is '오목'.

examples.en: She is pregnant, so her belly is rounded out.

examples.ko: 볼록한 유리 렌즈로 글씨를 크게 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw the letters bigger through a convex glass lens.
After the meal my belly was round.

examples.ko: 이 컵은 가운데가 볼록하고 입구는 좁아요.
examples.en: This cup bulges in the middle and has a narrow mouth.

examples.ko: 볼록한 거울은 넓은 곳을 비춰 줘요.
examples.en: A convex mirror shows a wide area.
His pocket was bulging, so I wondered what was inside.

explain: 배, 볼, 호주머니처럼 둥글게 나온 곳에 주로 써요. '볼록한'으로 꾸미고, 가운데가 들어간 것은 '오목하다'예요. 크게 불거지면 '불룩하다'를 써요.
explain_en: It is used for places that stick out round, such as a belly, cheek or pocket, and you modify nouns with '볼록한'. Something dented in is '오목하다', and something bulging a lot is '불룩하다'.

examples.ko: 불씨가 꺼지지 않게 장작을 더 넣었어요.
examples.en: I added more firewood so the embers would not die out.

examples.ko: 작은 불씨 하나가 큰 산불로 번졌어요.
examples.en: One small ember spread into a big forest fire.

examples.ko: 모닥불의 불씨를 물로 꼭 꺼야 해요.
examples.en: You must put out the embers of the campfire with water.
Grandmother left embers in the fireplace.
Without a lighter it was hard to get a spark going.

examples.ko: 불씨가 아직 살아 있어서 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: The embers are still alive, so we have to be careful.

explain: 불씨는 꺼지지 않고 남아 있는 작은 불이에요. 튀어 오르는 작은 불덩이는 '불똥'이라고 해서 서로 달라요. 비유로 큰 문제를 일으킬 작은 원인에도 써요.

phrases.example: 작은 오해가 큰 싸움의 불씨가 됐어요.
phrases.en: A small misunderstanding became the spark of a big fight.
phrases.nuance_ko: 큰 갈등이나 사건이 시작되는 작은 원인을 말할 때 비유로 써요. 싸움, 논란, 갈등과 자주 같이 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figure of speech for the small cause that starts a big conflict or incident. It often appears with fights, controversies and conflicts.

explain_en: 불씨 is a small fire that stays alive and can start a bigger one. '불똥' is different: it is a small flying spark. Figuratively, 불씨 is a small cause that can grow into a big problem.

examples.en: I shaved my head before going into the army.
After shaving my head, it felt cool.
He decided to shave his head to become a monk.
A cap suits a shaved head well.
I saw my son with a shaved head for the first time.

examples.ko: 야구부 학생들은 시즌 전에 삭발을 해요.
examples.en: The baseball team students shave their heads before the season.

explain: 삭발은 머리를 거의 밀어 버릴 때 쓰고, 보통 머리를 자를 때는 '이발'이나 '커트'를 써요. '삭발을 하다'로 말하고, 군대, 운동부, 스님, 굳은 각오를 보여 줄 때 자주 나와요.
explain_en: 삭발 is for shaving the head almost bald, while an ordinary haircut is '이발' or '커트'. You say '삭발을 하다'. It often comes up with the army, sports teams, monks, or showing strong resolve.

examples.en: My husband shaved his head because it is summer.
Everyone shaves their head when they join the army.

examples.ko: 스님은 출가할 때 삭발하고 절에 들어가요.
examples.en: A monk shaves his head and enters the temple when he leaves home.

examples.ko: 삭발할 용기가 없어서 그냥 짧게 잘랐어요.
examples.en: I lacked the courage to shave it, so I just cut it short.
We bet that the losing team would shave their heads.

examples.ko: 그 배우는 영화 때문에 삭발한 모습으로 나왔어요.
examples.en: The actor appeared with a shaved head for the film.

explain: '삭발'의 '발(髮)'이 이미 머리털이라는 뜻이라 보통 '머리를 삭발하다'보다 '삭발하다'만 말해요. 입말에서는 '머리를 밀다'가 더 가볍게 들려요. 스스로 할 때도, 남이 해 줄 때도 같은 말을 써요.
explain_en: The 발 (髮) in 삭발 already means hair, so people usually say just 삭발하다 rather than 머리를 삭발하다. In casual speech '머리를 밀다' sounds lighter. The same verb works whether you do it yourself or someone does it for you.

examples.en: Grandmother embroiders flowers on a handkerchief.

examples.ko: 어머니는 한 땀 한 땀 베개에 이름을 수놓으셨어요.
examples.en: Mother embroidered a name on the pillow stitch by stitch.
The stars dotting the night sky look beautiful.
I bought thread for embroidering in each color.
In autumn the maple leaves paint the mountain red.

examples.ko: 이 가방에는 작은 새가 수놓여 있어요.
examples.en: A little bird is embroidered on this bag.

explain: 천에 바늘과 실로 그림이나 글자를 만들 때 쓰고, '수를 놓다'라고 띄어 쓰기도 해요. 비유로 별, 꽃, 단풍이 가득 퍼진 모습에도 써서 '별이 하늘을 수놓다'라고 해요. 이때는 글이나 방송에서 더 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is used for making pictures or letters on cloth with needle and thread, and can also be written as two words, '수를 놓다'. Figuratively it describes stars, flowers or autumn leaves spread across a place, as in '별이 하늘을 수놓다', mostly in writing and broadcasts.

examples.en: My older brother rides a scooter to work.

examples.ko: 제주도에서 스쿠터를 빌려서 한 바퀴 돌았어요.
examples.en: I rented a scooter in Jeju and rode all the way around.
A scooter is smaller and lighter than a motorcycle.

examples.ko: 비가 오는 날에는 스쿠터를 타기 무서워요.
examples.en: I am scared to ride a scooter on rainy days.
A delivery scooter went through the alley.

examples.ko: 스쿠터를 탈 때는 헬멧을 꼭 써야 해요.
examples.en: You must wear a helmet when riding a scooter.

explain: 스쿠터는 바퀴가 작고 발을 올리는 판이 있는 가벼운 오토바이예요. 한국에서는 '오토바이'가 더 넓은 말이라 스쿠터도 오토바이에 들어가요. 아이들이 발로 차며 타는 것은 '킥보드'라고 불러서 서로 달라요.
explain_en: A 스쿠터 is a light motorbike with small wheels and a flat footboard. In Korea '오토바이' is the wider word, so a scooter counts as one too. The kind kids push with a foot is called '킥보드', which is different.

examples.ko: 다음 주에 한국어 교육 심포지엄이 열려요.
examples.en: A Korean language education symposium is held next week.
The professor gave a presentation at the symposium.
I signed up in advance to attend the symposium.
The topic of this symposium is the environment.

examples.ko: 심포지엄이 끝난 뒤에 점심을 같이 먹었어요.
examples.en: We had lunch together after the symposium ended.

examples.ko: 온라인 심포지엄은 집에서도 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can watch an online symposium from home.

explain: '세미나'와 비슷하지만 심포지엄은 여러 발표자가 한 주제를 나눠서 발표하는 행사예요. 주로 대학이나 학회에서 쓰는 말이라 일상 대화에서는 잘 안 나와요. '심포지엄을 열다', '심포지엄에 참석하다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is close to '세미나', but at a 심포지엄 several speakers each present on one shared topic. It is mostly used at universities and academic societies and rarely in daily talk. Typical phrases are '심포지엄을 열다' and '심포지엄에 참석하다'.

examples.en: For me the library is a haven for the mind.

examples.ko: 여행에서 돌아오면 집이 가장 편한 안식처 같아요.
examples.en: After a trip, home feels like the most comfortable refuge.

examples.ko: 힘들 때 숨을 수 있는 안식처 하나쯤은 필요해요.
examples.en: Everyone needs at least one refuge to hide in when things are hard.

examples.ko: 그 고양이는 우리 집을 안식처로 삼았어요.
examples.en: That cat made our house its home base.

examples.ko: 시골 마을에서 안식처를 찾았다는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people say they found a refuge in a country village.

examples.ko: 이 쉼터는 갈 곳 없는 사람들에게 안식처가 돼요.
examples.en: This shelter becomes a haven for people with nowhere to go.

explain: 몸과 마음이 편히 쉴 수 있는 곳에 써요. '피난처'는 위험을 피해 가는 곳이고, 안식처는 마음이 편해지는 곳이에요. 실제 장소뿐 아니라 사람, 책, 취미에도 비유로 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is for a place where body and mind can rest easy. A '피난처' is where you go to escape danger, while 안식처 is where you feel at peace. It is often used figuratively for people, books or hobbies as well as real places.

examples.ko: 어림으로 계산해도 대략 만 원쯤 나와요.
examples.en: Even by rough calculation it comes to about ten thousand won.

examples.ko: 제 어림에는 그 일이 한 시간이면 끝날 것 같아요.
examples.en: By my estimate, that job will be done in an hour.
Roughly a hundred people came.

examples.ko: 눈으로 어림을 해 보니 길이가 두 미터쯤 돼요.
examples.en: Eyeballing it, the length is about two meters.

examples.ko: 시험 점수를 어림해 보면 팔십 점 정도예요.
examples.en: If I estimate my test score, it is around eighty.
I walked on a rough guess and got lost.

explain: 어림은 정확하게 재지 않고 대충 짐작하는 것이라서 '어림잡다', '어림짐작'처럼 다른 말과 붙어서 자주 나와요. '대충'은 일을 성의 없이 할 때도 쓰지만, 어림은 수나 양을 짐작할 때 주로 써요.

phrases.en: You want to buy it at this price? No way.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대의 부탁이나 기대를 강하게 거절할 때 써요. 말투가 세서 친한 사이에서 주로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to firmly turn down someone's request or expectation. It sounds strong, so it is mostly said between people who are close.

explain_en: 어림 is rough guessing without measuring exactly, so it usually appears inside words like '어림잡다' and '어림짐작'. '대충' can also mean doing a job carelessly, but 어림 is mainly for guessing numbers or amounts.

examples.en: The fans cheered for the singer passionately.

examples.ko: 관객들은 공연이 끝나자 열렬히 박수를 쳤어요.
examples.en: The audience applauded enthusiastically when the show ended.
He loved her passionately.

examples.ko: 선수들을 열렬히 환영해 주는 사람들이 많았어요.
examples.en: Many people gave the players a warm, eager welcome.

examples.ko: 아이가 새 학교에 가기를 열렬히 바랐어요.
examples.en: The child eagerly wished to go to the new school.
My parents, who had strongly opposed it, finally agreed.

explain: 열렬히는 응원, 박수, 사랑, 환영, 반대처럼 마음이 크게 드러나는 말과 같이 와요. '열심히'는 노력하는 모습이고, 열렬히는 뜨거운 감정과 태도를 말해요. 대화보다 글이나 방송에서 더 자주 나와요.
explain_en: 열렬히 goes with words where strong feeling shows, like cheering, applause, love, welcome and opposition. '열심히' is about working hard, while 열렬히 is about burning emotion and attitude. It appears more in writing and broadcasts than in conversation.

examples.en: I had a formal outfit made to wear to the wedding.
Soldiers wear dress uniforms at ceremonies.

examples.ko: 예복은 평소 옷보다 단정하고 격식이 있어요.
examples.en: Formal wear is neater and more formal than everyday clothes.
I only wear this formal outfit at graduations.

examples.ko: 예복 때문에 너무 더워서 땀이 났어요.
examples.en: The formal clothes made me so hot that I sweated.
What is the difference between a suit and formal wear?

explain: 예복은 결혼식, 졸업식, 공식 행사처럼 격식 있는 자리에서 입는 옷이에요. '정장'은 직장에서도 입지만 예복은 특별한 행사 때 입어서 더 무거운 느낌이에요. 신부가 입는 옷은 '웨딩드레스', 신랑이 입는 옷은 '턱시도'나 '예복'이라고 해요.
explain_en: 예복 is clothing for formal occasions such as weddings, graduations and official events. A '정장' (suit) can be worn to work too, but 예복 is for special events, so it feels heavier. A bride's outfit is a '웨딩드레스', and a groom's is a '턱시도' or '예복'.

examples.en: I received an encouragement prize in the writing contest.
I am happy to get even an encouragement prize.

examples.ko: 아쉽게도 대상은 못 받고 장려상에 그쳤어요.
examples.en: Unfortunately I missed the grand prize and ended up with the encouragement prize.

examples.ko: 이번 공모전에서 제 친구가 장려상을 탔어요.
examples.en: My friend won an encouragement prize in this contest.
Winners of the encouragement prize get a book as a gift.

examples.ko: 장려상은 우수상보다 한 단계 낮은 상이에요.
examples.en: The encouragement prize is one level below the excellence prize.

explain: 장려상은 대상, 최우수상, 우수상 다음에 주는 상이에요. 열심히 한 사람을 격려하는 느낌이 있어서 '장려상을 받다'라고 해요. '참가상'은 참여만 해도 받는 상이라서 장려상과 달라요.
explain_en: 장려상 comes after the grand prize, '최우수상' and '우수상'. It has the feel of encouraging someone who tried hard, and you say '장려상을 받다'. A '참가상' is given just for taking part, so it is different.

examples.en: The whole school gathered on the playground.

examples.ko: 전교생이 백 명도 안 되는 작은 학교예요.
examples.en: It is a small school with fewer than a hundred students in total.
The teacher greeted the entire student body.

examples.ko: 이 학교는 전교생이 같이 소풍을 가요.
examples.en: At this school all the students go on a picnic together.
I was nervous receiving an award in front of the whole school.
The singing of the whole school could be heard in the classroom.

explain: 전교생은 한 학교 전체 학생이에요. '전교'만 붙이면 학교 전체라는 범위가 되어서 '전교 일등'처럼 써요. 한 반이나 한 학년 전체는 '반 학생들', '학년 전체'라고 말해요.
explain_en: 전교생 means every student of one school. The part '전교' alone sets the range to the whole school, as in '전교 일등' (first in the school). One class or one grade is '반 학생들' or '학년 전체'.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 김치 제조법을 공개하지 않아요.
examples.en: This shop does not reveal its kimchi recipe.

examples.ko: 할머니는 비누 제조법에 대해 잘 아세요.
examples.en: Grandmother knows a lot about how to make soap.

examples.ko: 제조법이 간단해서 집에서도 만들 수 있어요.
examples.en: The method is simple, so you can make it at home.

examples.ko: 이 치즈의 제조법은 아주 오래된 전통 방식이에요.
examples.en: The way this cheese is made is a very old traditional method.
After the method changed, the taste got better.
I looked up how to make natural cosmetics on the internet.

explain: 제조법은 공장이나 가게에서 물건을 만드는 방법이에요. 집에서 음식을 만들 때는 보통 '만드는 법', '요리법', '레시피'라고 해요. '비법'은 남이 모르는 특별한 방법이라서 제조법과 달라요.
explain_en: 제조법 is the method for making a product in a factory or shop. For cooking at home people usually say '만드는 법', '요리법' or '레시피'. A '비법' is a special secret method that others don't know, so it is different.

examples.en: He dropped out of university and started a business.
I dropped out of high school because of family circumstances.

examples.ko: 중퇴한 학생들이 다시 공부하는 학교가 있어요.
examples.en: There is a school where students who dropped out study again.
I worried for a long time about whether to drop out.
My friend is dropping out in order to work.
Many people succeeded even after dropping out of college.

explain: 학교를 졸업하기 전에 중간에 그만둘 때 쓰고, '대학을 중퇴하다'처럼 학교 이름 뒤에 '을/를'을 붙여요. 반대말은 '졸업하다'예요. 잠깐 쉬는 '휴학하다'와 달리 학교를 아예 그만두는 거예요.
explain_en: It is used when you leave school partway, before graduating, and you attach 을/를 to the school: '대학을 중퇴하다'. The opposite is '졸업하다'. Unlike '휴학하다', which is taking a break, 중퇴하다 means leaving school for good.

examples.ko: 회사에서 새 직원에게 지침서를 나눠 줬어요.
examples.en: The company handed out a manual to new employees.

examples.ko: 지침서에 안전 규칙이 자세히 나와 있어요.
examples.en: The safety rules are explained in detail in the guidebook.

examples.ko: 처음 쓰는 사람을 위한 지침서를 읽어 봤어요.
examples.en: I read a guidebook for first-time users.

examples.ko: 지침서대로 하면 실수를 줄일 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you follow the guidebook, you can make fewer mistakes.
The school made a new guide for exams.

examples.ko: 이 지침서는 너무 길어서 끝까지 못 읽었어요.
examples.en: This guidebook is so long that I could not read it to the end.

explain: 지침서는 일을 어떻게 해야 하는지 규칙과 순서를 적은 문서예요. 물건 쓰는 법을 적은 '설명서'와 달리, 일하는 방법과 지켜야 할 기준을 적어서 직장이나 기관에서 많이 써요. '매뉴얼'도 비슷한 뜻으로 써요.
explain_en: 지침서 is a document of rules and steps for how to do a job. Unlike a '설명서', which explains how to use a product, it sets out work methods and standards, so it is common in workplaces and organizations. '매뉴얼' is used in a similar sense.

examples.en: I poured hot tea into the teacup.
The teacup I got as a gift is so pretty.
I dropped the teacup and it broke.
I carefully placed the teacup in front of the guest.
A flower petal is floating in the teacup.
This teacup has no handle.

explain: 찻잔은 차를 마실 때 쓰는 잔이에요. 커피는 '커피잔', 물은 '컵'이나 '물잔'이라고 해서 마시는 것에 따라 이름이 달라요. 소리 나는 대로 [차짠]이라고 읽어요.

phrases.example: 그 논란은 찻잔 속의 태풍으로 끝났어요.
phrases.en: That controversy ended as a storm in a teacup.
phrases.nuance_ko: 크게 떠들썩해 보였지만 작은 범위 안에서만 일어나고 끝난 소동을 말해요. 뉴스나 신문에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a fuss that looked big but stayed within a small circle and then faded. Common in news and newspapers.

explain_en: A 찻잔 is the cup you drink tea from. Coffee goes in a '커피잔' and water in a '컵' or '물잔', so the name changes with the drink. It is read as [차짠].

examples.en: The street cleaner sweeps the road from dawn.
The building cleaner is mopping the hallway.
Thanks to the cleaners, the streets are clean.

examples.ko: 청소부께 아침마다 인사를 하면 기분이 좋아요.
examples.en: Greeting the cleaner every morning makes me feel good.
My friend's father works as a cleaner.
A cleaner's work is hard but absolutely necessary.

explain: 공식 글이나 뉴스에서는 거리 청소하는 사람을 '환경미화원'이라고 해요. 직접 부를 때는 '아저씨', '아주머니'가 자연스러워요. 청소부는 일을 낮춰 보는 느낌으로 들릴 수 있어서 조심해서 써요.
explain_en: In formal writing and news, people who clean the streets are called '환경미화원'. When addressing one directly, '아저씨' or '아주머니' sounds natural. 청소부 can sound as if it looks down on the job, so use it carefully.

examples.en: Hehe, actually I ate it first.
My friend giggled sheepishly and said sorry.

examples.ko: 칭찬을 받자 아이가 헤헤 하고 웃었어요.
examples.en: When praised, the child grinned happily.

examples.ko: 헤헤, 이거 제가 직접 만든 거예요!
examples.en: Hehe, I made this myself!
I was sleepy and just kept giggling.
My younger sibling ran off to the room giggling.

explain: 헤헤는 쑥스럽거나 기분이 좋아서 장난스럽게 웃는 소리예요. '하하'는 시원하게 크게 웃을 때, '히히'는 장난스럽게 웃을 때, 헤헤는 조금 멋쩍을 때 써요. 문자나 채팅에서 많이 쓰고 격식 있는 글에는 안 써요.
explain_en: 헤헤 is a playful laugh when you feel shy or pleased. '하하' is a hearty laugh and '히히' a mischievous one, while 헤헤 fits a slightly sheepish moment. It is common in texts and chats but not in formal writing.

examples.en: Soy-sauce marinated crab is called a rice thief.
Mixing rice into the marinated crab makes it tasty.

examples.ko: 게장은 간장으로 담그면 짭짤하고 양념으로 하면 매콤해요.
examples.en: Marinated crab is salty with soy sauce and spicy with seasoning.
I ate the marinated crab my mother made herself.

examples.ko: 게장을 먹고 나서 손에서 비린내가 났어요.
examples.en: After eating marinated crab my hands smelled fishy.
I ordered the marinated crab set meal at the restaurant.

explain: 게장은 게를 간장이나 양념에 절여서 먹는 반찬이에요. 간장으로 담근 것은 '간장게장', 매운 양념으로 한 것은 '양념게장'이라고 해요. 밥이 계속 들어가서 '밥도둑'이라는 별명이 있어요.
explain_en: 게장 is a side dish of crab cured in soy sauce or seasoning. The soy-sauce kind is '간장게장' and the spicy kind is '양념게장'. It has the nickname '밥도둑' (rice thief) because you keep eating more rice with it.

examples.ko: 길에서 차가 고장 나서 견인차를 불렀어요.
examples.en: My car broke down on the road, so I called a tow truck.

examples.ko: 견인차가 우리 차를 정비소로 끌고 갔어요.
examples.en: The tow truck pulled our car to the repair shop.
I parked illegally and my car was towed.
They say the tow truck driver will arrive soon.

examples.ko: 사고 현장에 견인차 두 대가 왔어요.
examples.en: Two tow trucks came to the scene of the accident.
The towing cost was more expensive than I thought, which surprised me.

explain: 견인차는 고장 난 차나 불법 주차한 차를 끌고 가는 차예요. 보험을 쓰면 '긴급 출동'이라는 서비스로 부르기도 해요. 입말에서는 '레커차'라고도 해요.
explain_en: A 견인차 tows away broken-down or illegally parked cars. With car insurance you can often call one as an '긴급 출동' (emergency dispatch) service. In casual speech it is also called '레커차'.

examples.en: The sound was so loud that my eardrums hurt.
The doctor checked my eardrum.

examples.ko: 귀를 세게 파면 고막이 다칠 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you dig at your ear hard, you can hurt your eardrum.

examples.ko: 비행기를 타면 고막이 답답할 때가 있어요.
examples.en: On a plane, my ears sometimes feel blocked.

examples.ko: 고막이 터질 것 같은 폭죽 소리였어요.
examples.en: The firecracker sound felt like it would burst my eardrums.

examples.ko: 고막은 소리를 듣는 데 중요한 역할을 해요.
examples.en: The eardrum plays an important role in hearing.

explain: 고막은 귀 안쪽에 있어서 눈에는 안 보이지만, 큰 소리가 날 때 말로 자주 나와요. '고막이 터질 것 같다'처럼 소리가 아주 클 때 과장해서 말하기도 해요. 병원에서는 '고막 검사'를 해요.
explain_en: The 고막 sits deep inside the ear, so you can't see it, but the word comes up often when a sound is loud. People exaggerate with '고막이 터질 것 같다' (my eardrums will burst). At the hospital there is a '고막 검사' (eardrum exam).

examples.en: My father was hospitalized from overwork.

examples.ko: 너무 과로하면 건강을 해칠 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you overwork too much, you can ruin your health.
I have a lot of work these days, so I overwork every day.

examples.ko: 과로한 날에는 저녁도 안 먹고 잠들어요.
examples.en: On days I overwork, I fall asleep without even eating dinner.

examples.ko: 과로하지 않도록 쉬는 시간을 꼭 가지세요.
examples.en: Make sure to take breaks so that you don't overwork.

examples.ko: 팀원들이 과로하는 모습을 보면 마음이 아파요.
examples.en: It hurts to see my teammates overworking.

explain: 과로하다는 몸이 견딜 만한 정도를 넘게 일할 때 써서 '피곤하다'보다 심각해요. '과로로 쓰러지다', '과로사'처럼 건강 문제와 이어져 자주 나와요. 더 가벼운 말로는 '무리하다'가 있어요.
explain_en: 과로하다 is for working past what your body can take, so it is more serious than '피곤하다'. It often links to health problems, as in '과로로 쓰러지다' and '과로사' (death from overwork). A lighter word is '무리하다'.

examples.en: He is just an observer watching the incident.

examples.ko: 관찰자의 눈으로 보면 문제가 더 잘 보여요.
examples.en: If you look through an observer's eyes, the problem is easier to see.
In the study an observer records the children's behavior.
I attended this meeting as an observer.

examples.ko: 좋은 관찰자는 작은 변화도 놓치지 않아요.
examples.en: A good observer doesn't miss even small changes.
I sat quietly like an observer and watched the people.

explain: 관찰자는 직접 하지 않고 곁에서 보며 살피는 사람이에요. '구경꾼'은 재미로 보는 사람이고, '목격자'는 사건을 직접 본 사람이에요. 관찰자는 연구나 회의처럼 일부러 살펴보는 자리에서 주로 써요.
explain_en: A 관찰자 watches closely from the side without taking part. A '구경꾼' watches for fun, and a '목격자' is someone who saw an incident firsthand. 관찰자 is mostly used where watching is deliberate, like research or meetings.

examples.en: You must not look down on people for their looks.
He looked down on me because I was young.
I studied hard so that no one could look down on me.
He underestimated his opponent and lost the match.
The belittling tone of voice made me feel bad.
I am upset because my friends look down on me.

explain: 깔보다는 상대가 나보다 못하다고 생각하며 낮게 볼 때 써요. '무시하다'는 상대의 말이나 존재를 신경 쓰지 않는 것이고, 깔보다는 마음속으로 낮게 보는 느낌이에요. '얕보다'도 비슷하게 써요.
explain_en: 깔보다 is used when you think the other person is lower than you. '무시하다' means ignoring someone's words or existence, while 깔보다 is the inner feeling of seeing them as beneath you. '얕보다' is used in a similar way.

examples.en: I was thirsty and drank the water in one gulp.
The child swallowed the pill in one gulp.
I was nervous and swallowed hard.

examples.ko: 쓴 약이었지만 눈을 감고 꿀꺽 넘겼어요.
examples.en: The medicine was bitter, but I closed my eyes and got it down in one gulp.

examples.ko: 그는 꿀꺽 소리가 크게 나도록 주스를 다 마셨어요.
examples.en: He drank all the juice with a loud gulp.

examples.ko: 동생이 내 간식을 몰래 꿀꺽해 버렸어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling secretly gobbled up my snack.

explain: 꿀꺽은 음식이나 물을 한 번에 크게 삼키는 소리와 모양에 써요. 여러 번 마시면 '꿀꺽꿀꺽', 조금씩 마시면 '홀짝홀짝'이라고 해요. 놀라거나 긴장했을 때 '침을 꿀꺽 삼키다'라고 하고, '남의 것을 말없이 가지다'는 뜻으로도 입말에서 써요.
explain_en: 꿀꺽 is the sound and look of swallowing food or water in one big gulp. Repeated gulps are '꿀꺽꿀꺽' and small sips are '홀짝홀짝'. When surprised or tense you '침을 꿀꺽 삼키다', and in casual speech it can also mean quietly taking something that is not yours.

examples.en: I failed the exam and was deeply discouraged.

examples.ko: 너무 낙담하지 말고 다시 해 봐요.
examples.en: Don't lose heart; let's try again.
I comforted my discouraged friend.

examples.ko: 그 소식을 듣고 낙담할 수밖에 없었어요.
examples.en: Hearing that news, I could not help but be disheartened.
He had a look of dismay on seeing the result.
People who don't lose heart even after failing are cool.

explain: 기대했던 일이 잘 안 되어서 힘이 빠질 때 써요. '실망하다'보다 마음이 더 무너지는 느낌이고, 말투가 조금 딱딱해요. 일상에서는 '속상하다', '힘이 빠지다'를 더 많이 말하고, 위로할 때는 '낙담하지 마세요'라고 해요.
explain_en: Used when something you hoped for fails and your energy drains. It feels like a heavier collapse of spirit than '실망하다' and sounds a bit stiff. In daily talk '속상하다' or '힘이 빠지다' are more common, and to comfort someone you say '낙담하지 마세요'.

examples.en: The ship dropped anchor in the harbor.
The sailors raised the anchor and set off.
The anchor caught on the bottom and the boat stopped.

examples.ko: 이 가게 로고는 작은 닻 모양이에요.
examples.en: This shop's logo is shaped like a small anchor.

examples.ko: 친구가 닻 모양 목걸이를 선물로 줬어요.
examples.en: My friend gave me an anchor-shaped necklace as a gift.

examples.ko: 폭풍이 오자 닻을 더 깊게 내렸어요.
examples.en: When the storm came, they let the anchor down deeper.

explain: 닻은 배가 흘러가지 않게 물속으로 내리는 무거운 쇠 도구예요. 배를 멈출 때는 '닻을 내리다', 출발할 때는 '닻을 올리다'라고 해요. 한곳에 자리 잡고 정착하는 것도 비유로 '닻을 내리다'라고 말해요. 소리는 [닫]이에요.
explain_en: A 닻 is the heavy iron tool lowered into the water so a ship won't drift. You stop with '닻을 내리다' and set off with '닻을 올리다'. Figuratively '닻을 내리다' also means settling down in one place. It is pronounced [닫].

examples.en: A vine is growing along the fence.
I rested for a while under the grapevine.
The vine wraps around the tree and climbs up.
Small pumpkins grew on the pumpkin vine.
A rose vine covered the wall.

examples.ko: 덩굴을 자르지 않으면 집을 다 덮어요.
examples.en: If you don't cut the vine, it will cover the whole house.

explain: 포도, 호박, 장미처럼 줄기가 길게 뻗거나 다른 것을 감고 자라는 식물에 써요. '덩굴'과 '넝쿨'은 둘 다 표준어예요. '덩쿨'은 틀린 표기라서 조심하세요.
explain_en: It is used for plants like grapes, pumpkins and roses whose stems stretch long or wind around other things. Both '덩굴' and '넝쿨' are standard words. '덩쿨' is a wrong spelling, so watch out.

examples.en: The guard called a coworker on the walkie-talkie.
At the construction site they contact each other by walkie-talkie.
I can't hear the walkie-talkie well.
The children play with a toy walkie-talkie.
The walkie-talkie battery has run out.

examples.ko: 산에서는 휴대폰이 안 터져서 무전기를 챙겨 갔어요.
examples.en: Phones don't work in the mountains, so I took a walkie-talkie.

explain: 무전기는 휴대폰 없이 가까운 사람과 바로 말할 때 쓰는 기계예요. 말할 때 버튼을 누르는 방식이라 '무전을 치다', '교신하다'와 같이 써요. '라디오'는 듣기만 하지만 무전기는 말도 할 수 있어요.
explain_en: A 무전기 lets you talk straight to someone nearby without a phone. You press a button to speak, and it goes with '무전을 치다' and '교신하다'. A '라디오' only receives, but a 무전기 can also transmit.

examples.en: He is a gourmet who knows good restaurants well.
Many gourmets visit this restaurant.

examples.ko: 저는 미식가는 아니지만 맛있는 음식을 좋아해요.
examples.en: I'm not a gourmet, but I like delicious food.
I wanted to become a gourmet, so I learned cooking.
I prepared food to suit a gourmet's taste.

examples.ko: 친구는 미식가라서 식당을 고를 때 까다로워요.
examples.en: My friend is a gourmet, so he is picky choosing restaurants.

explain: 미식가는 음식 맛을 잘 알고 맛있는 것을 찾아다니는 사람이에요. '식도락가'는 먹는 즐거움을 더 강조하고, '먹보'는 많이 먹는 사람이에요. 칭찬으로 쓰지만 '입이 까다롭다'와 비슷하게 들릴 때도 있어요.
explain_en: A 미식가 knows food well and seeks out good meals. '식도락가' stresses the pleasure of eating, and '먹보' is a person who eats a lot. It is meant as praise, but it can sometimes sound like '입이 까다롭다' (picky).

examples.en: Grandmother came with clothes wrapped in a cloth bundle.

examples.ko: 장사꾼이 보따리를 풀어 물건을 보여 줬어요.
examples.en: The peddler untied his bundle and showed his goods.
While moving I tied the small things up in a bundle.
I met a traveling peddler at the market.

examples.ko: 보따리가 너무 무거워서 들 수 없었어요.
examples.en: The bundle was too heavy to lift.
After the trip I came back with a bundle full of gifts.

explain: 보따리는 천으로 물건을 싸서 묶은 짐이에요. 옛날에는 가방 대신 썼고, 지금도 '보따리 장수'나 '이야기 보따리'처럼 남아 있어요. 등에 지는 것은 '봇짐'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: Grandfather started to unpack his bag of old stories.
phrases.nuance_ko: 재미있는 이야기를 많이 꺼내 놓을 때 써요. 이야기가 가득 든 보따리를 푸는 모습에서 나온 비유예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone starts telling lots of interesting stories. It comes from the image of untying a bundle full of stories.

explain_en: A 보따리 is a load wrapped in cloth and tied. People used it instead of a bag in the past, and it survives in '보따리 장수' (traveling peddler) and '이야기 보따리' (bag of stories). One carried on the back is a '봇짐'.

examples.en: A typhoon is moving north toward Korea.

examples.ko: 벚꽃 전선이 북상하면서 꽃이 피고 있어요.
examples.en: The cherry blossoms are opening as the bloom front moves north.
The rain clouds are moving north, so take an umbrella.
The heat is moving north, so Seoul will get hot too.
I saw news that the typhoon is moving north.

examples.ko: 장마 전선이 북상할 때는 비가 많이 와요.
examples.en: It rains a lot when the rainy-season front moves north.

explain: 태풍, 장마, 꽃 소식처럼 날씨와 자연이 북쪽으로 올라올 때 주로 일기예보와 뉴스에서 써요. 반대로 남쪽으로 내려오는 것은 '남하하다'라고 해요. 사람이 걸어서 북쪽으로 갈 때는 잘 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: It is mainly used in weather forecasts and news when a typhoon, rainy front or blooming moves up to the north. Moving down south is '남하하다'. It is rarely used for a person walking north.

examples.en: The pyramids are truly mysterious structures.
That incident is still a mystery.
Strange, unexplainable things happened one after another.
There are many puzzling phenomena in nature.

examples.ko: 과학으로 설명할 수 없어서 더 불가사의하게 느껴져요.
examples.en: It can't be explained by science, so it feels all the more mysterious.
I read about the seven wonders of the world in a book.

explain: 이해하거나 설명할 수 없을 만큼 이상하고 놀라울 때 써요. '신기하다'는 가벼운 놀라움이고, 불가사의하다는 이유를 알 수 없는 큰 수수께끼 같은 느낌이에요. 글에서 많이 쓰고, '세계 7대 불가사의'처럼 명사 '불가사의'로도 써요.
explain_en: It is used when something is so strange and amazing that it can't be understood or explained. '신기하다' is light wonder, while 불가사의하다 feels like a big riddle with no known reason. It is common in writing and also works as the noun '불가사의', as in '세계 7대 불가사의'.

examples.en: Running water has come to the country village too.

examples.ko: 상수도 요금은 두 달에 한 번 내요.
examples.en: I pay the water bill once every two months.
The water was cut off because of waterworks construction.

examples.ko: 상수도는 강물을 깨끗하게 만들어서 집으로 보내 줘요.
examples.en: The water supply cleans river water and sends it to homes.
A water main burst and the road was flooded.

examples.ko: 이 지역은 아직 상수도 시설이 부족해요.
examples.en: This area still lacks water supply facilities.

explain: 상수도는 깨끗한 물을 집과 건물로 보내 주는 시설이에요. 쓰고 난 더러운 물을 내보내는 시설은 '하수도'라서 둘을 한 쌍으로 말해요. 집에서는 '수도', '수돗물'이라고 줄여서 말해요.
explain_en: 상수도 is the system that sends clean water to homes and buildings. The system that carries away used dirty water is '하수도', so the two are talked about as a pair. At home people shorten it to '수도' and '수돗물'.

examples.en: I heard the whisper of the wind in the forest.
My heart pounded at his whisper.

examples.ko: 아이들의 속삭임 때문에 수업이 조금 시끄러웠어요.
examples.en: The children's whispering made the class a little noisy.

examples.ko: 도서관에서는 속삭임처럼 작은 소리로 말해야 해요.
examples.en: In the library you must speak as quietly as a whisper.
The sound of whispering grew louder.
I was startled when I heard my friend's whisper.

explain: 속삭임은 작게 소곤소곤 말하는 소리와 그 분위기에 써요. '귓속말'은 남이 못 듣게 귀에 대고 하는 말이고, 속삭임은 소리 자체를 말해요. '바람의 속삭임'처럼 시나 노래에도 자주 나와요.
explain_en: 속삭임 is the sound and mood of speaking softly in a low voice. A '귓속말' is words said into someone's ear so others can't hear, while 속삭임 is about the sound itself. It also appears often in poems and songs, like '바람의 속삭임'.

examples.en: The front gate is tied up with a chain.
The puppy was tied to a chain.
I locked my bike to the post with a chain.
The chain was so heavy that my hands sweated.
In the movie the prisoner was wearing chains.
The chain rusted and snapped.

explain: 쇠사슬은 쇠고리를 이어서 만든 줄이에요. '체인'과 같은 뜻이지만 자전거 체인이나 가게 이름 같은 곳에서는 '체인'을 더 많이 써요. 자유를 막는 것을 비유로 말할 때는 '사슬'이나 '속박'을 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: 쇠사슬 is a line made of linked metal rings. It means the same as '체인', but for bike chains or store chains people mostly say '체인'. For something that restricts freedom, '사슬' or '속박' are used figuratively.
